key_insight: Changing the source-to-substrate distance (15–24 cm) tunes the thickness, band gap, and semiconducting behavior of thermally evaporated CdTe, CdSe, and Sb2S3 thin films.
engineering_relevance: The results suggest SSD is a simple process knob for optimizing absorber-layer films, with CdTe and especially CdSe showing promise for thin-film solar cell applications.
method: Thermal evaporation of CdTe, CdSe, and Sb2S3 thin films at SSDs of 15, 18, 21, and 24 cm
Characterized structure and composition using XRD and EDX
Evaluated thickness, optical band gap, transmittance, and electrical behavior
evidence_signal: XRD showed polycrystalline CdTe/CdSe and amorphous Sb2S3, while optical analysis found only marginal band-gap shifts but a clear thickness decrease as SSD increased.
watch_item: These are laboratory-scale thin films, so device-level solar-cell performance and long-term stability still need direct validation.
paper_title: Effect of Source-to-Substrate Distance on the Optical and Electrical Properties of Thermally Deposited CdTe, CdSe and Sb$_2$S$_3$ Thin Films
